messages:
sec-bot: [ALERT] Image scan detected HIGH severity CVE (CVE-2026-XXXX) in layer of runtime base image `runtime/base:6-buster` (sha256:9f2a...). Affected deployed image: `runtime/service-runtime:v3.2.3` used in prod-us-east-1 and staging-us-west-2.
Mike: saw it, thanks. paging infra oncall @ops-oncall — can you confirm if prod is using the exact sha? :eyes:
Jess: running SBOM lookup now: `sbomctl query --image sha256:9f2a... --format=json` — gives openssl 1.1.1 package in layer 4.
Sara: confirmed: service-runtime:v3.2.3 is pinned to sha256:9f2a... in prod deployment.
Raj: immediate containment: I'll add a deny rule to Artifact Registry to block pushes and deployments of that digest and update the k8s admission controller to reject `runtime:v3.2.3` for now.
Mike: ops, should we rollback to v3.2.2 or patch in-place? impact estimate?
ops-oncall: starting rollback to runtime:v3.2.2 in prod now. updating deployment image, will watch healthchecks. I've also added a temporary policy in Artifact Registry to block new pulls of the affected digest.
Jess: adding this CVE to vuln-triage board and creating an emergency SBOM update. Also searching for other images that include the same libssl layer: `registry-scan --match-layer sha256:abcd...`
sec-bot: Audit note: image push events show last push for sha256:9f2a... at 1779899000 by service account `ci-runner@redwood-ci.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. No external IPs flagged yet.
Sara: question: do we rotate the signing KMS keys used for image provenance? signing key is in GCP KMS keyring `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/prod/cryptoKeys/signing`.
Mike: let's not rotate KMS keys blind. Raj, confirm whether the artifact was signed by the expected CI service account and whether the CI credential was compromised. If push origin is legitimate, rotate deploy tokens and tighten RBAC on the registry.
Raj: checking audit logs for pushes and IAM grants. Preliminary: pushes from legitimate CI runner from internal IPs. Will still rotate the GitHub Actions deploy token and tighten Artifact Registry IAM bindings (remove all-users for read/pull).
Jess: I'll draft internal comms and a short customer note ready in case escalates. For now INTERNAL ONLY. Also scheduling a rebuild pipeline to produce a patched image with openssl patched to 1.1.1t and new SBOM.
ops-oncall: rollback finished at 1779900284. Traffic fully shifted to v3.2.2, error rate back to baseline. No ongoing incidents.
Sara: remediation plan: 1) rebuild images with patched dependency, 2) sign with rotated KMS key, 3) publish new SBOM, 4) update admission controller to require SBOM + valid signature, 5) run full registry-wide layer scan for same libssl layer.
Mike: created incident ticket INC-2026-341, assigned owners: Jess (comm & postmortem), Raj (audit, RBAC), Sara (remediation & SBOM), ops-oncall (rollback & monitor).
Jess: adding automated weekly registry scan to detect similar layer matches and adding a policy to block deploys if installed CVEs > HIGH.
Raj: I'll also run a one-off IAM review for Artifact Registry & KMS keys and revoke any stale service accounts.
Mike: agree on post-incident sync tomorrow 09:30 UTC. Good catch by scanner — thanks team. :thumbsup:
sec-bot: Incident state: CONTAINED. Follow-ups documented in INC-2026-341.
